subject: math

objective.text: A kilogram is 1000 grams. Break a kilogram into 10 parts of 100 grams, then 10 grams, then 1 gram.

explanations.title: A kilogram
explanations.text: A kilogram is a unit for measuring weight. We write it as kg.

explanations.title: A pan balance
explanations.text: A pan balance is level when both sides weigh the same. A 1 kg bag of beans balances a 1 kg weight.

explanations.title: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams
explanations.text: Split 1 kg into 10 equal parts. Each part is about 100 grams. Count 100, 200, up to 1000.

explanations.title: Like place value
explanations.text: 10 grams make 10 tens of 1 gram. 10 parts of each unit make the next bigger unit, just like place value.

source_ref.section: Concept Development, Part 2 and Problem Set item 5 (place value charts)

examples.title: Take out 100 grams
examples.text: The bag has 1000 grams. Scoop out 100 grams. 900 grams are left in the bag.

questions.text: Count by 5 minutes from 12. What do you say when you reach the 7?

source_ref.section: Fluency: Tell Time on the Clock

questions.text: One pan has a 1 kg weight. The other has a 1 kg bag of beans. How do you know it is balanced?
A 1 kg bag is split into 10 equal parts. About how many grams is each part?
How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
The bag has 1000 grams. You scoop out 100 grams. How many grams are still in the bag?
Now the bag has 900 grams. Will it balance the 1 kilogram bag of beans?
A cup has 100 grams of rice. You scoop 10 grams into a smaller cup. How many grams are left in the first cup?
Ten bags of sugar weigh 1 kilogram. How many grams does each bag weigh?
A 10-gram weight is on a pan balance. How many 1-gram weights balance it?
A kilogram weight is on a pan balance. How many 100-gram weights balance it?
10 one-gram weights balance 10 grams. 10 ten-gram weights balance 100 grams. What pattern do you see?
How are kilograms and grams alike? How are they different?
